background.summary: Existing models exhibit failures such as binding attributes to the wrong objects, fusing objects, and producing spatial relations or counts that differ from the prompt.

evidence.quote: Existing models exhibit failures such as binding attributes to the wrong objects, fusing objects, and producing spatial relations or counts that differ from the prompt.

However, conventional models, which receive no explicit information about syntactic structure, are given the same word sequence under both interpretations; the user therefore cannot specify the intended interpretation, and which interpretation is depicted is left to the model.

solution.summary: In this section, we propose CCG Diffusion, which extends Predicated Diffusion by integrating CCG parsing.
solution.approach: In this section, we propose CCG Diffusion, which extends Predicated Diffusion by integrating CCG parsing.
components: CCG Diffusion parses the input prompt with a CCG parser.

Using the syntactic information in the resulting derivation, it reduces errors in attribute binding, spatial relations, and object counts in compositional text-to-image generation and disambiguates PP attachment in syntactically ambiguous prompts according to the specified interpretation.
It achieves both in a unified manner and without additional training of the image generation model.

experiments.summary: In the attribute-binding categories, our method achieves the highest scores among all methods on both backbones.

evidence.quote: In the attribute-binding categories, our method achieves the highest scores among all methods on both backbones.
It significantly outperforms all other methods in all three categories on Stable Diffusion and in shape on Sana.
